This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

2. The petition averments briefly stated as under; That on 06.02.2024 at about 4.00 p.m. petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider on Scooter bearing Reg.
SCCH-5 No.KA-13-FZ-5742 being ridden by its rider on NH-75 B.M.Road, Nuggenahalli Cross Circle, Hirisave Town, Hassan, at that time, a Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C- 0882 being driven by its driver at a very high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the said scooter.
Due to the impact, petitioner fell down and sustained multiple injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to Government Hospital, Channarayapatna, after first aid, she was shifted to Punya Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient and spent a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and other incidental charges.
3. At the time of the accident, petitioner was aged about 20 years, hale and healthy, working as Tailor and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to do any work as she was doing prior to SCCH-5 the accident.
With regard to accident in crime No.19/2024 is registered against the driver of the said offending car before the Hirisave Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the R.C.Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.
Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared through counsel and filed written statement.

Further submitted that, respondent No.2 has issued a commercial vehicle policy of issuance under policy No.6301167696 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-0882 and same is valid from 17.12.2023 to 16.03.2024 and liability SCCH-5 of this respondent is limited to terms and conditions of the policy.
Respondent No.2 seeks protection under Sec.147 and 150 M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, driver of the car was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and the driving licence was suspended from 09.11.2023 to 08.05.2024 and the alleged accident was occurred on 06.02.2024 and also submitted that, insured vehicle did not had valid permit and fitness to ply on the road.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following:
Neethu C K vs Pradeep on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161270730/
2 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 06.02.2024 at about 4.00 p.m. on SCCH-5 NH-75 BM Road, Nuggenahalli Cross Circle, Hirisave Town, Hassan due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-0882 dashed against the petitioner Scooter and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?

sentences.text: 3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner herself examined as PW-1 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13.

On the other hand, Manager -Legal Claims of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1, Superintendent, Rajajinagar RTO as RW-2 and marked 4 documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.
7.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
SCCH-5 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:
::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the case, petitioner examined herself as PW-1, in her chief- examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated.

In order to prove road traffic accident PW-1 produced and marked copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2,
copy of crime details form as Ex.P.3, copy of sketch as Ex.P.4, copy of seizure mahazar as SCCH-5 Ex.P.4, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.8.
9.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and documents those have marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 corroborates the case of the petitioner about occurrence of the road traffic accident dated 06.02.2024 and injuries sustained by petitioner as alleged in the petition.
10. Per contra, Manager-Legal claims of respondent No.2 is examined as RW-1 and marked as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy as Ex.R.2.
R.W.1 stated that as on the date of accident the driver of offending car was not holding valid driving licence as the same was suspended from 09.11.2023 to 08.05.2024.
During the cross examination of R.W.1, she denied the suggestion regarding existence of driving licence of driver of offending car.

SCCH-5 Neethu C K vs Pradeep on 6 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161270730/
3 11.
Further examined Superintendent, Rajajinagar RTO as RW-2 and marked authorization letter as Ex.R.3, copy of D.L.Extract of Mohan Kumar as Ex.R.4.
As per Ex.R4 the driving licence of Mohan Kumar was suspended between 09.11.2023 and 08.05.2024.
R.W.2 specifically stated that during the suspension of driving licence the driver cannot drive the vehicle.
During the cross examination of R.W.2 nothing is elicited to version of R.W.2.
Thus it is clear that as on the date of accident the driving licence of car bearing registration No.KA-13- C-0882 was under suspension and he not permitted to drive the vehicle.
Respondent No.2 not disputed the manner of accident and injuries sustained by the petitioner.

In the absence of iota of evidence, this tribunal held that the petitioner sustained the injuries due to the accident occurred on 06.02.2024 at about 4.00 p.m. SCCH-5 when she was travelling as a pillion rider on Scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-13-FZ-5742 on NH-75 BM Road,
Nuggenahalli Cross Circle, Hirisave Town, Hassan.
12. It is evident from police papers that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of driver of the car bearing Reg. No.KA-13-C-0882.
Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained scalp injury and fracture pelvis right hip and she took conservative treatment.

To prove the said injuries and treatment taken by her, petitioner has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.7, discharge summary marked as SCCH-5 Ex.P.10 issued by Punya Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient from 06.02.2024 to 11.02.2024 i.e., for a period of 5 days.

Further she has furnished medical bills for Rs.52,448/- as Ex.P.11, medical prescriptions as Ex.P.12, CT-Scan films as Ex.P.13.
14.

As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 20 years, for proof of her age, she has produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.9, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner as 13.12.2004 and the alleged accident is occurred on 06.02.2024, accordingly relying on Ex.P.9 her age is considered about 20 years as on the date of accident.
Further petitioner has contended that, she is working was tailor, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

To prove the said fact,
there are no documents on record.
SCCH-5 15.
It is admitted fact that, as per the discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10, petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 06.02.2024 to 11.02.2024 at Punya Hospital i.e., for 5 days.
Further admittedly petitioner has exhibited Ex.P.11 medical bills for Rs.52,488/-.
On perusal of the said bills it is clearly stated about spending of amount for this treatment is concerned.
Further on perusal of Ex.P.7 in which Doctor who have treated has categorically stated that, petitioner has sustained grievous injury out of the accident caused on 06.02.2024.

So as per Ex.P.7 wound certificate,
petitioner has sustained fracture pelvis right iliac bone, which is grievous in nature.
Further the Investigation Officer has also filed charge sheet against Mohan Kumara for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 of IPC.

So the said charge sheet materials and SCCH-5 evidence of PW-1 clearly states that, petitioner is suffering from grievous injury out of the accident caused in the alleged accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

sentences.text: In the absence of rebuttal evidence about the injuries sustained by petitioner merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case.

Considering the nature of the injuries sustained, treatment taken and medical expenses incurred by the petitioner, she is entitled for global compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- which includes medical bills of Rs.52,488/-.

17. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

18. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Car bearing Reg. No.KA-13- C-0882 which was valid from 17.12.2023 to 16.03.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 06.02.2024 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force but the driving licence of driver of car was under suspension as on the date of accident thereby the respondent No.1 violated the terms and conditions of policy.

Hence respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
within 60 days from the date of this order with liberty to recover the same from respondent No1 as per law.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.

SCCH-5 19. Issue No.3: For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.2,50,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.1 with due process of law.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
SCCH-5 Draw award accordingly.
